paragraphs.text: A growing number of popular cities now charge visitors a small tax for each night they stay. In my opinion, this is one of the fairest ways to deal with the pressures that tourism creates.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Residents of these cities pay for the streets to be cleaned, the buses to run and the old buildings to be repaired, yet visitors use all of these services too. A charge of a few euros a night is unlikely to change anyone’s travel plans, but across millions of visitors it can raise large sums.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The difficulty lies in how the money is spent. Too often it disappears into general budgets, and residents see no improvement. I would argue that the income should be clearly linked to projects that tourists and residents can both see.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Some hotel owners fear that the tax will send visitors to cheaper destinations. It is possible that very price-sensitive travellers will choose elsewhere, but the cities with the highest taxes remain among the most visited in the world.
paragraphs.label: D

items.prompt: The writer considers a nightly tourist tax to be fair.
The writer thinks a small nightly charge will persuade many tourists to change their plans.
The writer believes the tax should be the same in every city.
The writer suggests that the money should pay for projects people can see.
The writer accepts that the tax might discourage some travellers.
